clue.text: It's extraordinary to be so incompetent

definitions.meaning: split in two, the answer says a person is '...', so unfit for the task

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at how remarkably incompetent another person is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable stands out; read as two words, the answer also means lacking the ability, which is incompetence.

clue.text: Gets inside information coming up for savings

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
inside means the word Gets is placed within the word for information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone acquires insider tips that help build up their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts GETS within GEN, giving GGETSEN; 'coming up' turns that over to read NESTEGG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside for the future, a sum of savings.

clue.text: Sobbing, having finally got a scolding

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word got

parts.note: an earful is a telling-off, a scolding

explanation.surface: Someone was in tears after at last receiving a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sobbing is crying, with tears running down.

clue.text: Muslim lady to show hesitancy in speech after press is seen

indicators.note: after puts the hesitation sound behind the word for press

parts.note: to press someone is to beg or urge them
um is the noise a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: A Muslim woman hesitates when speaking once the press turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: A begum is a Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia; 'press' looks like journalists but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Begum is a title for a Muslim woman of rank, chiefly in South Asia.

clue.text: Record membership at the start of the student year

definitions.text: Record membership at the start of the student year

parts.words: Record membership at the start of the student year
parts.note: describes the signing-up of new students onto the books when term begins

explanation.surface: A college logs how many students have joined as the academic year opens.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing on as a member of a college or course, registration, happens at the start of the year.

clue.text: Trip and fall following initial slip

indicators.note: following puts the word for fall behind that letter
initial picks out the opening letter of the word slip

parts.note: a tumble is a fall

explanation.surface: Someone trips and falls after first slipping.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to catch one's foot and lurch, to lose footing.

clue.text: Approximately one thousand held captive in WWI battle

indicators.note: held captive means one piece is enclosed inside the other

parts.note: some can mean about or roughly, as in 'some twenty people'
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Around a thousand men were taken prisoner in a First World War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme was a major 1916 offensive on the Western Front, named after the French river.

clue.text: Continued, strangely, to be missed

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of Continued are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: Something carried on, oddly enough, without anyone spotting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something missed has gone unseen, escaping attention.

clue.text: Shaw's major character

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw wrote a play whose heroine holds the rank of Major in the Salvation Army; 'major' reads as an adjective but is her rank

explanation.surface: A critic names the principal role in a Shaw play.
explanation.definitionFit: Major Barbara is a 1905 Shaw play named for its heroine, a Salvation Army officer.

clue.text: Retired Thespian appearing as Shylock

parts.note: ex means former, so retired
a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: A former actor takes the stage as Shakespeare's moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock is the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, who demands his pound of flesh; here it stands for anyone who exacts payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A shylock is a harsh moneylender, one who demands payment ruthlessly.

clue.text: Brag about scrambled raw eggs

indicators.note: scrambled says the letters of raw eggs are mixed up, as eggs are in a pan

explanation.surface: Someone boasts about the raw eggs they have scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger is to strut and boast, which is bragging.

clue.text: Junior accountant's holiday spot

parts.note: minor means younger or junior
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A junior accountant chooses where to spend the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Minorca is a Spanish island in the Balearics, popular with British holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca, a Balearic island in the Mediterranean, is a popular resort destination.

clue.text: At home in France

parts.note: asks for the French phrase meaning with the family, at home

explanation.surface: Someone is at home in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means within the family, so at home and informally.

clue.text: Pamphlet followed by pronouncement

indicators.note: by pronouncement says a word is said aloud and the entry is its sound-alike

parts.note: to have tracked someone is to have followed them

explanation.surface: A leaflet was then followed by an official statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short leaflet, often religious or political, a pamphlet.

clue.text: A number love to be included in break dance

indicators.note: to be included in places the number and love inside the word for break

parts.note: a gap is a break
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a number
love is zero in tennis, looking like the letter O

explanation.surface: Some dancers form a couple to perform in a break dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The galop is a lively 19th-century ballroom dance in quick two-time.
explanation.definitionFit: The galop is a fast ballroom dance in two-time, popular in the 1800s.

clue.text: Cut paying, produce hostility

indicators.note: produce means make something new from the letters of Cut paying

explanation.surface: Slashing someone's pay breeds bad feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Pugnacity is readiness to fight, aggressive ill will.

clue.text: Ideal item for a beginner at a furniture factory?

definitions.text: Ideal item for a beginner at a furniture factory?

parts.words: Ideal item for a beginner at a furniture factory?
parts.note: a novice furniture maker would want a seat that is simple to build

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a new worker at a furniture works should make first.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a comfortable armchair; read literally, a chair that is no trouble to make.

clue.text: Lusty punishment

definitions.meaning: a beating with a leather belt

explanation.surface: A vigorous thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapping lad is robust and hearty; a strapping is also a thrashing with a belt.

clue.text: Soldiers embark in combat plane built to take cargo

indicators.note: embark in means the soldiers board, going inside the aircraft

parts.note: a fighter is a combat aircraft
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops board a warplane designed for carrying cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the vessel by its purpose: a ship or aircraft built to carry goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a ship or aircraft designed for carrying goods rather than passengers.

clue.text: Revised list for a retailer in a growing trade

definitions.text: a retailer in a growing trade

indicators.note: revised says the letters of list for are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An updated list is drawn up for a shopkeeper in an expanding business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing trade' looks like a booming business, but means one that sells things that grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A florist sells flowers and plants, things that literally grow.

clue.text: Watch the dance in which one has a pupil

definitions.meaning: to look hard at, stare at

definitions.text: the dance in which one has a pupil
definitions.meaning: split as a ball (dance) held by the organ of sight, which contains a pupil

explanation.surface: Observing the dance where one partners a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' reads as a student partnered at a dance, but is the dark centre of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball is to stare at; the eye's globe contains the pupil.

clue.text: Yes — Russian tea may be found here

definitions.text: Yes — Russian tea may be found here

parts.note: da is Russian for yes
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Agreed: Russian tea is to be had at this place.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country cottage, where Russian tea would be served.

clue.text: Hazel's hangers-on

parts.note: reads like a woman's hangers-on, but describes the dangling flower spikes of the hazel tree

explanation.surface: A woman named Hazel and her retinue of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Catkins are the drooping flower clusters that hang from hazel and willow branches.

clue.text: Feeling guilty, has made reparations

indicators.note: reparations, read as re-parations, says the letters of has made are put back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A guilt-ridden person has paid compensation for wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ashamed is to feel embarrassment or guilt over what one has done.

clue.text: Work time in the music business

parts.note: op, short for opus, labels a numbered musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone works a stint in the music industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a whole branch of the musical world, staged musical drama and its trade.

clue.text: Afrikaans is imitated in tough paper

indicators.note: in means the imitation piece sits within the word for tough paper

parts.note: cutch is a tough paper used by goldbeaters between gold leaves
aped means copied or imitated

explanation.surface: Afrikaans is copied onto sturdy paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Dutch was the old name for Afrikaans, the language of South Africa's Dutch settlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Dutch is an old name for the South African language that grew from Dutch.

clue.text: Communist firm about belief

indicators.note: about means the word for firm goes round the communist

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A firm set up by communists holds a particular faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a statement of faith.

clue.text: Approach shown by a forceful person

definitions.meaning: a private road leading up to a house
energy and ambition, which a go-getter displays

explanation.surface: A method shown by a dynamic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is the road up to a house; it is also the push and ambition of a go-getter.

clue.text: One drink swallowed by Miss West in picture

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: swallowed by means the drink goes down inside the actress's name

parts.note: Mae West was a Hollywood actress
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: In a film, Mae West downs a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to see it in the mind, to conjure it up.

clue.text: It provides good tips for writers

definitions.text: It provides good tips for writers

parts.words: It provides good tips for writers
parts.note: reads like advice for authors, but means a hard metal used for the points of fountain-pen nibs

explanation.surface: Something offers useful advice to authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridium, a hard corrosion-resistant metal, is used for the tips of pen nibs.

clue.text: Cry when people meet

parts.note: a greeting-like shout, but the meet is a foxhunt gathering and the cry is the huntsman's call on sighting the fox

explanation.surface: People call out to each other as they get together.
explanation.walkthrough: A meet is the gathering of a foxhunt; the huntsman shouts this on sighting the fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the hunting call raised when the fox is spotted at a hunt.

clue.text: Fancied one at the party, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says a word is said aloud and the entry sounds like it

parts.note: a guest is someone attending a party

explanation.surface: Someone was attracted to a person at the party, so the rumour goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to suppose or surmise it, so to have made a guess.
